newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco extends GSM phone links to remote areas.
newsitem.headline: Morocco extends GSM phone links to remote areas.

text.p: Morocco, which plans to soon privatise its GSM mobile telephone system, has extended the network to remote areas in northern, central and southern provinces, an official source said on Tuesday.

The state Office National des Postes et Telecommunications (ONPT) extended the GSM network to "11 provinces located in northern, central and southern areas of Morocco, including Casablanca suburbs," the source said.
The extension aims at developing new services and reinforcing the modernisation of Morocco's telecommunications, he said.
Morocco has an estimated 30,000 subscribers to the GSM system introduced during the meeting of the General Agreement on Trade and Tariffs (GATT) in Marrakesh in 1994.
The GSM network has since been concentrated mainly around the big cities.
The extension follows recent government approval partly to privatise the telecommunications sector, including the GSM mobile telephone network, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
A government draft law is expected to be presented this month for adoption by the existing 333-seat parliament.
South Korean giant Daewoo, the U.S. AT&T and French Alcatel companies have shown interest in the privatisation of the GSM system, the stockbroker said.
Earlier this year, the ONPT said it would invest $1.5 billion over the next five years to expand and improve the telephone network.
With its 27 million population, Morocco has a tele-density of four percent, or four phone lines per 100 inhabitants.
